title: Unemployment Benefit Claims Weeks over Which a Dependency Disallowance Reduction Runs
content:
For a dependency disallowance on an Unemployment Benefit Claims record, the reduction runs for a number of weeks that depends on the weekly payments already issued on the claim and on its remaining balance. Weekly payments are the payment entries of the weekly kind issued on the claim. The weekly amount used here is the weekly benefit amount plus the dependency allowance on the claim before the disallowance.

| Weekly payments issued on the claim | Remaining balance | Weeks the reduction runs for |
|---|---|---|
| None | Any | The program's maximum duration weeks less its waiting week count |
| One or more | Below 4 weeks of the weekly amount (the late-balance weeks) | The remaining balance divided by the weekly amount, rounded up to the whole week |
| One or more | At least 4 weeks of the weekly amount | The program's maximum duration weeks |

Rounding up to the whole week counts any part of a week as a week: a quotient of exactly 2 stays 2, while a balance 0.01 above two weekly amounts gives 3.

## Hypothetical cases (weekly benefit amount 346.00, allowance on the claim 45.00, so a weekly amount of 391.00 and a late-balance line of 1564.00)

| Weekly payments issued | Remaining balance | Weeks |
|---|---|---|
| None | Any | For a program with 26 maximum duration weeks and a waiting week count of 1: 25 |
| 10 | 1000.00 | 1000.00 divided by 391.00 is about 2.56: 3 |
| 10 | 782.00 | Exactly 2 |
| 10 | 1564.00 | Not below the line: the maximum duration weeks |
